findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.title: HAR Multi-Scale — 4 HAR variants overwhelmingly beat GJR-GARCH (DM=-15.45)
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.how_strengthens: Paper claims GARCH defines a daily-frequency floor. K530 shows HAR with |r| proxy SHATTERS this floor (DM=-15.45). This CONTRADICTS the complexity ceiling claim for volatility forecasting but STRENGTHENS it for VT strategy (K533 shows HAR is worse for VT). Needs nuanced treatment.
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: UPDATE Complexity Ceiling table to add row: 'GJR → HAR-ABS: QLIKE improves massively (DM=-15.45) but VT strategy WORSENS.' This actually strengthens the ceiling's main point that better prediction ≠ better investment decisions.

findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.title: HAR Cross-Asset — 7/7 assets all beat GJR-GARCH, HAR advantage is UNIVERSAL
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.how_strengthens: Validates that HAR universally dominates GARCH for pure forecasting across ALL 7 assets tested. Strengthens the paper's nuance: the complexity ceiling is about INVESTMENT DECISIONS, not STATISTICAL MEASUREMENT. Currently the paper only mentions HAR indirectly.
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: ADD 1-2 paragraphs in Complexity Ceiling section acknowledging HAR as the true QLIKE champion while reinforcing that this forecasting superiority does not translate to VT improvement (K533).

findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.title: Prediction ≠ Application #5 — HAR best predictor but worst VT strategy
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.how_strengthens: CRITICAL supporting evidence for the paper's central thesis that better statistical measurement doesn't improve investment decisions. HAR-ABS has the best QLIKE (DM=-15.45 vs GJR) but the WORST VT Sharpe (1.123 vs 12/VIX's 1.748). 12/VIX remains irreplaceable.
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: ADD as a key example in the Complexity Ceiling discussion. This is perhaps the single strongest piece of evidence for the ceiling proposition.

findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.title: HAR-EVT is the only model passing complete Trinity Test for VaR
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.how_strengthens: Refines the VaR narrative: while Student-t improves VaR broadly, HAR-EVT is the ONLY specification passing both 1% and 2.5% VaR. Strengthens the three-domain framework: (i) GARCH eq for QLIKE, (ii) distributional assumption for VaR, (iii) VIX for strategy. HAR-EVT belongs to domain (ii).
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: UPDATE VaR section or Complexity Ceiling to note HAR-EVT as the domain (ii) optimal solution. Adds nuance without contradicting the ceiling.

K534 shows the correlation structure is VIX-regime dependent but UNSTABLE across decades, which paradoxically supports static 50/50 (dynamic optimization can't track shifting correlation).
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: ADD footnote or brief paragraph in Cross-Asset VT section explaining the VIX-regime dependence of SPY-GLD correlation as theoretical support for static allocation.

findings_that_ADD_new_sections.new_content: When VIX<15, lever to 1.5x; when VIX>25, 1.0x. Sharpe +0.112, CAGR +5.4%. Harvey DM t=7.90, JKM z=6.05. 11/11 cross-OOS wins. 100% bootstrap win rate. 25/25 sensitivity configs safe. Borrowing breakeven 9.7%. Survives 8% interest rate.
findings_that_ADD_new_sections.recommended_action: ADD new subsection in Discussion. This is the session's most validated finding and represents a genuine alpha source BEYOND the standard 12/VIX framework. Must be presented as an EXTENSION (not replacement) of the base VT framework.

findings_that_ADD_new_sections.title: Optimal Weight Function — 12/VIX is return-optimal, nonlinear only improves risk
findings_that_ADD_new_sections.new_content: Systematic comparison of 7 function families, 427 configurations. 12/VIX produces the HIGHEST return (12.5%/yr). Piecewise achieves highest Sharpe (1.803) but at 9.4% return — it trades return for lower vol. Linear c=10-14 produces a Sharpe flat curve. Nonlinear forms are preference choices, not dominance improvements.
findings_that_ADD_new_sections.recommended_action: EXPAND IVT subsection to include this systematic function comparison. Currently the paper treats 12/VIX as simply 'parsimonious' — K568 shows it is actually RETURN-OPTIMAL, a much stronger claim.

findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.title: Prediction ≠ Application #5 — HAR best predictor but worst VT strategy
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.how_strengthens: Provides another dimension to the 'VT ≠ trend following' argument. Not only is VT mechanically different from TSMOM, but the best STATISTICAL predictor (HAR) makes the WORST VT strategy. This means VT's value is NOT about prediction quality — it's about VIX-level-based position sizing, which HAR cannot replicate.
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: ADD as supporting evidence in the discussion of why VT ≠ trend following. 'A parallel test confirms this separation: the statistically best volatility forecaster (HAR-ABS, DM=-15.45 vs GJR) produces the worst VT strategy (Sharpe 1.123 vs 12/VIX's 1.748), because prediction accuracy and position-sizing effectiveness operate through different channels.'

This makes the insurance analogy QUANTITATIVELY precise.
findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: EXPAND Section 4.3 with the precise cost decomposition and breakeven VIX. The breakeven at VIX=26.6 is a publishable finding that strengthens the insurance framing.

findings_that_STRENGTHEN_existing_claims.recommended_action: ADD brief mention of VIX regime forward returns in Section 4.2 to explain WHY the insurance premium is paid (and why it's a fair price).
